newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA FINE BOSNICH FOR PRE-MATCH WALKOUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA FINE BOSNICH FOR PRE-MATCH WALKOUT.

text.p: Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich was heavily fined by manager Brian Little on Monday for walking out on the team before Villa's English premier league match at Derby on Saturday.

The Australian international keeper stormed out of the dressing room and away from Derby's Baseball Ground an hour before the kick-off when he found out his deputy Michael Oakes was playing instead of him. Derby won the game 2-1.
A Villa spokesman said Bosnich had apologised to Little and the club, but added: "He has been fined heavily but we are not saying how much the fine is."
Bosnich was fined 1,000 pounds ($1,600) by the English F.A. for making a Hitler-style salute at Tottenham fans during Villa's match at White Hart Lane last October.
He had been expected to be recalled for next Saturday's match against Tottenham at Villa Park, but Little is now expected to keep him sidelined for the time being.

While Bosnich was being fined for his walkout, first division rivals Bolton and Wolves were heavily fined by the F.A. for a brawling during their match at Burnden Park on January 18 which Bolton won 3-0.
Both clubs admitted charges of misconduct and failing to control their players when they appeared before a disciplinary commission.
Bolton, who have since clinched the first division title, were fined 40,000 pounds ($65,000) of which 30,000 pounds ($49,000) has been suspended until the end of next season.
Wolves, also in the hunt for promotion to the Premiership, will have to pay less, having being fined 30,000 pounds ($49,000), with 22,500 pounds ($37,000) suspended.
